title: Geometric irreducible component counts commute with arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. For $t\in Y$ let $X_t$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre over the residue field $\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field]. For any separably closed field extension $K/\kappa(t)$ [def-pc-field-extension, def-pc-separably-closed], let $n_{X/Y}(t)$ be the number of irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum], with value $\infty$ if there are infinitely many. This value is independent of the separably closed extension $K$. If $g:Y^\prime\to Y$ is any scheme morphism and $X^\prime=X\times_Y Y^\prime$, then $n_{X^\prime/Y^\prime}(t^\prime)=n_{X/Y}(g(t^\prime))$ for every $t^\prime\in Y^\prime$. No finite type, flatness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: For a point $t\in Y$, put $k=\kappa(t)$ and choose separably closed extensions $K/k$ and $L/k$. By [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] choose a field $M$ with compatible embeddings of $K$ and $L$ over $k$. Since $K$ is separably closed, [lem-weil-pbc-field-tensor-irreducible] applied with base field $K$, field extension $M/K$, and an arbitrary field extension $E/K$ shows that $M\otimes_KE$ has a unique minimal prime; therefore $\operatorname{Spec}M$ is geometrically irreducible over $K$ by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Apply [lem-sc-product-irreducible-components-bijection] to the product of $\operatorname{Spec}M$ with $X_t\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$ over $K$. Its projection induces a bijection between irreducible components of $X_t\times_k\operatorname{Spec}M$ and those of $X_t\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$. The same argument over $L$ gives a bijection between the components over $M$ and those of $X_t\times_k\operatorname{Spec}L$. Composing one bijection with the inverse of the other proves equality of the component counts, including the empty and infinite cases; hence the value is independent of the chosen separably closed extension.

proof.text: Fix $t'\in Y'$ and write $t=g(t')$ and $k=\kappa(t)$, $k'=\kappa(t')$. The residue-field map [def-weil-residue-field] makes $k'$ a field extension of $k$. Choose separably closed extensions $K/k$ and $L/k'$. Regard $L$ also as a field extension of $k$ and apply [lem-weil-common-extension-fields] to obtain a field $M$ receiving compatible embeddings of $K$ and $L$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product], together with $X'=X\times_YY'$, identifies $((X'_{t'})_L)_M$ with $(X_t)_M$: a map to either scheme is exactly a compatible pair of maps to $X$ and $\operatorname{Spec}M$ over $Y$, with the map through $Y'$ forced by $\operatorname{Spec}M\to\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k'\to Y'$. It also identifies $(X_t)_K$ with the corresponding $K$-base change used in the definition of $n_{X/Y}(t)$.

source.place: Tag 0556, proof: comparison diagram of the two geometric fibres over a common separably closed field.

proof.text: The common field $M$ need not be separably closed. Since $K$ and $L$ are separably closed, [lem-weil-pbc-field-tensor-irreducible] applied to $M\otimes_K E$ for every field extension $E/K$, and likewise over $L$, shows that $\operatorname{Spec}M$ is geometrically irreducible over each base [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Thus [lem-sc-product-irreducible-components-bijection] gives a bijection from the components of $(X_t)_M$ to those of $(X_t)_K$ and a bijection from the components of $((X'_{t'})_L)_M$ to those of $(X'_{t'})_L$. The canonical isomorphism of Step 2 identifies the two source schemes. Their component counts therefore agree, including zero and infinity. By Step 1 the counts on the two target schemes are respectively $n_{X/Y}(t)$ and $n_{X'/Y'}(t')$, proving the required equality for every $t'$.

lean.statement: theorem geometricFibreComponentCount_baseChange {X Y : Scheme.{max u v}} (f : X ⟶ Y) : (∀ (t : Y) (K L : Type v) [Field K] [Field L] [IsSepClosed K] [IsSepClosed L] (i : Y.residueField t ⟶ CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} K)) (j : Y.residueField t ⟶ CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} L)), ENat.card (irreducibleComponents ↥(pullback f (Spec.map i ≫ Y.fromSpecResidueField t))) = ENat.card (irreducibleComponents ↥(pullback f (Spec.map j ≫ Y.fromSpecResidueField t)))) ∧ (∀ (Y' : Scheme.{max u v}) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (t' : Y') (K L : Type v) [Field K] [Field L] [IsSepClosed K] [IsSepClosed L] (i : Y.residueField (g t') ⟶ CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} K)) (j : Y'.residueField t' ⟶ CommRingCat.of (ULift.{u} L)), ENat.card (irreducibleComponents ↥(pullback (pullback.snd f g) (Spec.map j ≫ Y'.fromSpecResidueField t'))) = ENat.card (irreducibleComponents ↥(pullback f (Spec.map i ≫ Y.fromSpecResidueField (g t')))))
